title: New test_role_absent_demand_inert double-frees `trimmed` (new bad free @ catalog.odin:982 in `odin test core`)
evidence:
core/demand_test.odin:530-541:
	trimmed := make([dynamic]Demand_Entry, 0, 4, context.allocator)
	defer delete(trimmed)
	...
	delete(e3.entries)
	e3.entries = trimmed

core/catalog.odin:982 (inside catalogs_destroy):
			delete(cat.demand.eras[i].entries)
Runtime proof — HEAD `odin test core`: "+++ bad free        @ 0x649001478 [catalog.odin:982:catalogs_destroy()]"; base commit aec3c88 `odin test core` shows only the two pre-existing "[health_test.odin:867...]" / "[health_test.odin:900...]" bad frees, no catalog.odin one.
detail: Defer LIFO runs `delete(trimmed)` before `catalogs_destroy(cat2)`, which frees `e3.entries == trimmed` again. Delta-introduced double free (UB); suite still exits green, so no gate catches it.
recommended_fix: Drop `defer delete(trimmed)` — once `e3.entries = trimmed`, catalogs_destroy(cat2) owns the array (the original entries are already singly deleted).

title: W9 re-pin documents 'the CAMPUS half must land fully' but only asserts campus spawns > 0
evidence:
core/demand_test.odin:579 (test comment): "The honest floor is per-role: the CAMPUS half must land fully (campuses are"
core/demand_test.odin:727-728 (the only campus-half asserts):
	testing.expectf(t, campuses >= 1, "the honest surge floor requires a campus to exist (got %d) — a campus-silent pass is a regression", campuses)
	testing.expectf(t, campus_window_spawns > 0, "the honest surge floor requires a campus to SOURCE in the window (got %d in-window campus spawns)", campus_window_spawns)
detail: The per-role floor is stated as 'campus half lands fully' (PR body: 'measured 100%') but no fraction is pinned — a regression landing 1 campus spawn of the 18000 honest ask still passes W9 green.
recommended_fix: Assert the campus half's landing fraction, e.g. `campus_window_spawns >= 10*WINDOW*95/100` (measured 100%), next to the total MIN_LAND assert.

title: test_terminal_class_profiles hardcodes SURGE_AT=1200 while the same fold's W9 re-pin derives the window from data
evidence:
core/demand_test.odin:445: "	SURGE_AT :: u64(1200) // the streaming surge's data start_tick"
core/demand_test.odin:630-633 (same commit, W9): "	surge := &cat.demand.eras[2].set_pieces[0]
	SURGE_START := u64(surge.start_tick)" with comment "...so a future re-tune of the surge timing cannot silently drift this pin." (data/demand.json set-piece: start_tick 1200, duration 1800)
detail: The base/surge split boundary is hardcoded; a future surge-timing re-tune silently mislabels both windows in the class-profile test — exactly the drift class W9's derive-from-data fix was made to prevent.
recommended_fix: Derive SURGE_AT the same way W9 does (`cat.demand.eras[2].set_pieces[0].start_tick`) so the split tracks the data.
